catalogue.score_meaning: Subjective testing priority, NOT probability of success, recognition accuracy or empirical validation score. Scores are assigned before this batch is computed.
catalogue.scope: Geometry of the three user-labelled photo groups. No identity, ethnicity or anatomical ground truth is inferred.
catalogue.common_claim: The proposed descriptor improves later-month worst-pair date-median AUC by at least 0.02 over the best existing descriptor selected on early months, while retaining neutral/strict/pose-adjusted worst-pair AUC >= 0.65 and later-month AUC >= 0.70.
catalogue.priority_rubric: Priority reflects relevance to the previous eye/nose/brow findings, geometric interpretability, complementary information, computability from the verified cache and potential nuisance cancellation. It is not a calibrated confidence scale.
catalogue.novelty_policy: New explicit definitions, not guaranteed independent factors. Exact and near numerical duplicates of the previous 259 definitions and of this batch are reported, not hidden.

hypotheses.title: Horizontal skewness of visible aperture mass
hypotheses.rationale: Previous opening ratios were useful; mass skew adds the distribution of opening along the complete lid contour instead of another height ratio.
hypotheses.risk: Blinking, gaze and contour interpolation.

hypotheses.title: Kurtosis of visible aperture mass
hypotheses.rationale: Distinguishes broad from concentrated opening profiles with the same average aperture.
hypotheses.risk: Higher moments amplify landmark errors.

hypotheses.title: Upper versus lower lid shape variance
hypotheses.rationale: Separates contributions of the two lid contours rather than their pooled opening.
hypotheses.risk: Small lower-contour variance can destabilize a ratio.

hypotheses.title: Relative interquartile aperture spread
hypotheses.rationale: A robust shape-spread statistic may retain eye information while reducing sensitivity to single landmarks.
hypotheses.risk: It may be nearly redundant with an existing opening ratio.

hypotheses.title: Within-frame superellipse profile exponent
hypotheses.rationale: Fits contour shape within each frame, without labels; separates profile shape from absolute opening.
hypotheses.risk: The superellipse approximation may be poor.

hypotheses.title: Upper/lower lid mass-centre phase offset
hypotheses.rationale: Continuous mass centres avoid the jumping discrete apex features in older definitions.
hypotheses.risk: Gaze and asymmetric squinting.

hypotheses.title: Upper/lower lid profile concordance
hypotheses.rationale: Tests whether the two full curves carry stable coordinated shape beyond their mean separation.
hypotheses.risk: Nearly constant contours make correlation unreliable.

hypotheses.title: Medial/lateral curvature-energy balance
hypotheses.rationale: Local bending distribution differs from whole-eye tilt, mean arc length and simple bow.
hypotheses.risk: Polynomial differentiation amplifies contour noise.

hypotheses.title: Binocular normalized profile discrepancy
hypotheses.rationale: Whole-curve asymmetry may reveal information not present in point-aperture asymmetry.
hypotheses.risk: May primarily measure expression or image quality.

hypotheses.title: Binocular aperture-mass phase asymmetry
hypotheses.rationale: Tests distributional asymmetry independently of different absolute eye sizes.
hypotheses.risk: Previous simple asymmetries were weak; this is a high-priority falsification test.

hypotheses.title: Modelled medial/lateral opening concentration
hypotheses.rationale: The existing 134-point metrics mostly summarize height/area; distribution along the ordered contour is additional information.
hypotheses.risk: 3DMM-inferred eyelid geometry.

hypotheses.title: Intrinsic lid-loop warping
hypotheses.rationale: Best-plane residual measures nonplanarity, not plane orientation or raw depth spread; valid planar loops remain valid inputs.
hypotheses.risk: A model surface proxy, not measured orbital anatomy.

hypotheses.title: Lateral versus medial canthal wedge difference
hypotheses.rationale: Endpoint tangent wedges are distinct from whole-fissure tilt and average bow.
hypotheses.risk: End tangents may be sensitive to landmark spacing.

hypotheses.title: Double-row brow thickness taper
hypotheses.rationale: The six verified paired distances encode a gradient; existing offsets mostly average them.
hypotheses.risk: Modelled brow rows do not measure hair or bone thickness.

hypotheses.title: Brow-to-upper-lid clearance gradient
hypotheses.rationale: A profile gradient introduces spatial clearance, rather than another centroid distance.
hypotheses.risk: Requires ordered, consistently matched row progress.

hypotheses.title: Nasal sidewall waist
hypotheses.rationale: The middle of three verified bilateral widths can capture taper nonlinearity beyond alar width.
hypotheses.risk: Sidewall samples are not alar landmarks.

hypotheses.title: Internal root-tip-base rotation
hypotheses.rationale: The 51-54-60 angle is independent of the mouth-based nasolabial proxy and complements nasal width.
hypotheses.risk: Depth is inferred from a frontal image.

hypotheses.title: Basal nose-arc wrap
hypotheses.rationale: The 58-59-60-61-62 arc adds base curvature to the existing chord width.
hypotheses.risk: Five model samples provide only a coarse arc.

hypotheses.title: Malar protrusion-vector direction
hypotheses.rationale: Direction of the anterior-cheek/zygion proxy vector adds orientation instead of another depth difference.
hypotheses.risk: Mean-BFM reference vertices are soft-tissue proxies.

hypotheses.title: Malar vertical placement within the midface
hypotheses.rationale: Cheek position in the eye-line-to-subnasale interval adds location rather than global width/height.
hypotheses.risk: Age and reconstruction fitting remain confounded.

hypotheses.title: Visible eye-opening/nasal-aspect contrast
hypotheses.rationale: Opening and nasal aspect showed complementary group trends; a shared-source contrast can reinforce them.
hypotheses.risk: Both cues can change with pitch and expression.

hypotheses.title: Conservative opening/cantho-alar contrast
hypotheses.rationale: A lower-quantile opening with an inner-canthal nasal reference reduces dependence on extremes and face outline.
hypotheses.risk: The two normalizers may introduce correlated noise.

hypotheses.title: Root binocular aperture area over nasal width
hypotheses.rationale: Combines both eyes with the nasal width that already carried complementary information; all lengths share a pixel frame.
hypotheses.risk: Area remains expression-sensitive.

hypotheses.title: Visible ocular/nasal-loop area ratio
hypotheses.rationale: Area-to-area cancellation removes isotropic image scale and couples two distinct central regions.
hypotheses.risk: The nasal loop is a landmark contour, not segmentation.

hypotheses.title: Harmonic binocular opening over IPD-normalized alae
hypotheses.rationale: A harmonic bilateral estimate suppresses one excessively open or noisy eye while retaining nasal contrast.
hypotheses.risk: A genuinely closed eye can dominate the estimate.

hypotheses.title: Opening over root-alar triangular area
hypotheses.rationale: A central triangular reference avoids unstable face-outline normalization and introduces nasal height as well as width.
hypotheses.risk: A projected triangle is not a 3D anatomical area.

hypotheses.title: Aperture skew and nasal-midline bend interaction
hypotheses.rationale: Tests complementary distributional eye/nose shape instead of another rescaled mean opening.
hypotheses.risk: Interaction can amplify noise; no success probability is implied.

hypotheses.title: Aperture exponent versus nasal projective spacing
hypotheses.rationale: Couples two size-independent internal shape descriptors rather than gross facial lengths.
hypotheses.risk: Projection of non-collinear nose landmarks is approximate.

hypotheses.title: Nasal/ocular covariance-anisotropy balance
hypotheses.rationale: Whole-contour elongation balance may be less sensitive to individual landmark errors than endpoint ratios.
hypotheses.risk: Contour covariance is only a surface-shape proxy.

hypotheses.title: Aperture shape spread with nasal-width context
hypotheses.rationale: Adds an independent region to a robust within-eye shape statistic.
hypotheses.risk: Interaction may not improve the weakest pair.

hypotheses.title: Visible brow-canopy clearance gradient
hypotheses.rationale: Dense matched-position clearances test information beyond the old single-point brow distances.
hypotheses.risk: Brow grooming and expression.

hypotheses.title: Visible brow-canopy relative curvature
hypotheses.rationale: Curvature of the full clearance profile is distinct from mean height and tangent angle.
hypotheses.risk: Sparse eyebrow landmarks and grooming.

hypotheses.title: Visible double-row eyebrow taper
hypotheses.rationale: Uses verified upper/lower arcs instead of the older erroneous same-arc thickness sample.
hypotheses.risk: It measures a visible brow envelope, not bone.

hypotheses.title: Brow taper over nasal-sidewall waist
hypotheses.rationale: Couples two local model-shape gradients while cancelling global mesh scale.
hypotheses.risk: A weak taper may add no information.

hypotheses.title: Brow-clearance gradient over basal nose wrap
hypotheses.rationale: Combines spatial orbital clearance with a distinct nasal contour rather than common face width.
hypotheses.risk: Both quantities are inferred model contours.

hypotheses.title: Malar placement over conservative modelled aperture
hypotheses.rationale: Tests eye/cheek placement jointly; mean eye size already separated these groups.
hypotheses.risk: Age and fitted expression can affect both terms.

hypotheses.title: Malar direction with sidewall-waist context
hypotheses.rationale: Introduces a nasal shape context for a cheek-vector direction instead of another raw depth measure.
hypotheses.risk: A model-specific angular composite.

hypotheses.title: Brow ridge relief over conservative eye aperture
hypotheses.rationale: The promising ridge-depth cue gains a local orbital reference rather than global face width alone.
hypotheses.risk: Model depth and aperture fitting may share bias.

hypotheses.title: Malar placement over nasal aspect
hypotheses.rationale: Couples cheek location with nasal geometry that showed complementary group structure.
hypotheses.risk: Can reflect acquisition-period differences.

hypotheses.title: Full visible brow-clearance/nasal-height proportion
hypotheses.rationale: A robust full-profile measurement and central nasal reference avoid single brow points and face outline.
hypotheses.risk: Visible eyebrows are expression/grooming dependent.

hypotheses.title: Affine canthal tip/base area ratio
hypotheses.rationale: A ratio of triangle areas sharing a canthal base is invariant to an invertible 2D affine transform.
hypotheses.risk: A real rotated 3D face is not exactly an affine image warp.

hypotheses.title: Affine inner-canthal tip/root area ratio
hypotheses.rationale: Tests relative central nasal placement without separate horizontal/vertical scale assumptions.
hypotheses.risk: A nearly zero root triangle can be unstable.

hypotheses.title: Affine inner-canthal root-tip-base cross-area ratio
hypotheses.rationale: Products of area ratios cancel the common affine determinant while using four distinct central points.
hypotheses.risk: Nonplanar face projection and small triangles.

hypotheses.title: Affine binocular cantho-nasal cross-area ratio
hypotheses.rationale: Tests a bilateral affine invariant distinct from simple eye spacing or global canthal tilt.
hypotheses.risk: May be dominated by small asymmetries.

hypotheses.title: Dual-model ocular/nasal height consensus
hypotheses.rationale: Combines complementary visible and identity-mesh estimates, each normalized within its own coordinate frame.
hypotheses.risk: Systematic inter-model calibration bias remains.

hypotheses.title: Dual-model ocular/nasal area consensus
hypotheses.rationale: A shared-source area contrast in each model may preserve signal while reducing one-model noise.
hypotheses.risk: Corresponding landmark areas are proxies, not identical physical surfaces.

hypotheses.title: Dual-model medial/lateral aperture concentration
hypotheses.rationale: Checks whether independently estimated full-profile shape can support a more stable concentration descriptor.
hypotheses.risk: Landmark sampling and expression differ across models.

hypotheses.title: Relative ocular/nasal inter-model disagreement
hypotheses.rationale: A high-priority falsification/quality hypothesis: disagreement may explain apparent group separation or missing transfer.
hypotheses.risk: Quality/source bias, not necessarily a useful anatomical descriptor.

hypotheses.title: Binocular-consistency moderated dual-model contrast
hypotheses.rationale: Downweights bilateral contour inconsistency without learning label-specific weights.
hypotheses.risk: The quality penalty is heuristic and must be tested.

hypotheses.title: Visible flat-top opening over modelled nasal waist
hypotheses.rationale: Couples a new visible profile-shape cue with a new local modelled nasal taper cue.
hypotheses.risk: A hybrid of expression-sensitive and inferred geometry.

protocol.orientation: fixed from early dates, not reselected in bootstraps/permutations
protocol.bootstrap_unit: calendar month clusters of date medians
protocol.primary_association_correction: Bonferroni50; maxT conditional global-null comparison also reported

geometry_notes.normalization: Each source uses its own pupil/iris spacing; no raw MP/3D coordinate subtraction.
geometry_notes.eye_frame: lateral-to-medial chord; normal points upper-to-lower, fixing y-up/y-down and mirrored-side traps.
geometry_notes.canopy_matching: shared projected canthal abscissa, not unmatched point-by-point rows
geometry_notes.plane_validity: second singular value rejects collinearity; a valid planar loop has zero warping

limitations: Priority90-98 is subjective testing priority. It is not a calibrated posterior, success probability or empirical90% score.
The same three groups and later months were seen in earlier research. This is an internal exploratory batch, not an untouched prospective test.
Dates are supplied filename annotations. Calendar months only approximate independent acquisition sessions.
Group-label permutations assume exchangeability of month blocks under the null. Different periods/cameras/lighting can violate that assumption.
Association after Bonferroni50 or maxT does not establish incremental AUC improvement or anatomical causality.
Paired percentile-bootstrap difference intervals, including Bonferroni nominal simultaneous intervals, are approximate with few month blocks and a nonsmooth worst-pair statistic.
Only three groups; udmurt has13 neutral and5 strict-neutral photos. External generalization and90% empirical quality are not established.
3DMM contours and mean-selected cheek vertices are inferred surface proxies, not measured orbital/bony anatomy.
Eye opening, visible brow shape and iris placement depend on expression, gaze and grooming. Neutral flags are only blendshape thresholds.
Ratios of2D areas are affine invariant mathematically; the projection of a rotating nonplanar3D face is not generally a2D affine warp.
All50 frozen claims, failed tests and numerical/rank redundancies are retained. A new name is not evidence of new information.
The benchmark was selected using early-month robustness only, not the best old feature discovered after looking at later-month AUC.
No identities or sensitive traits are inferred. AUC is a dataset-label rank statistic, not a same/different-person verdict.
